question: Can GRAVITY's daily #1 be shorted at $500K–$1M without moving the price — and keep its accuracy?
method: Walk-forward, out of sample: monthly test folds, 5-session embargo (20 for multi-day holds), isotonic calibration on a later held-out slice — the production recipe.
Every variant was chosen on a DEVELOPMENT window (Dec 2024 – Oct 2025) and reported on an untouched CONFIRMATION window (Nov 2025 – Sep 2026), so picking the best of many cannot inflate the result.

Capacity: ≤ 5% of the session's expected dollar volume per leg and ≤ 0.5% estimated one-way impact (square-root law, Y = 0.7, daily volatility), using a conservative next-session volume (25th percentile after volume spikes), and, live, IBKR's lendable shares.
Costs: impact on both legs + an Abdi–Ranaldo effective-spread estimate (+ borrow fee for multi-day holds).

About 20 model variants tested: production features; new liquidity / intraday-habit features; bagging; liquid-only training; the pre-market gap (M1); dump-minus-pump ranking; direct return models; protective stops at 3–10%; 5/10/20-session holds; and a point-in-time universe.
verdict: Micro-caps (today's #1): the dumps are real, but these names trade so little that even ~$50K moves the price about as much as the dump. They are small-size trades — use each pick's capacity and breakeven size.

Names that can take $500K–$1M: the model still finds dump candidates at ~5× the normal rate, but they also rip; across every intraday variant the average move is too small to pay ~1.5–2.5% round-trip costs at that size. Protective stops did not fix it.

20-session shorts in liquid names looked excellent (+6–12% per trade) — until the universe was made point-in-time. Today's small-cap list over-represents stocks that already collapsed; with that bias removed the edge disappears. It was not shipped as a strategy.

The same correction trimmed the main #1's backtest while its ranking power was unchanged. Retrained on the point-in-time universe, the published #1 now backtests at 46% dumped 5%+ and -2.8% average open→close (median -4.3%), versus 9.2% for the average name. These are the numbers the site now reports.

Bottom line: no tested approach kept the micro-cap dump rate at $500K+ size. GRAVITY now shows, for every pick, how much it can absorb and what your size would cost, so the decision is yours with the real numbers in front of you.
main_pit_note: Experiment (dump-only recipe, development / confirmation periods) that motivated the switch; the official retrained numbers are in the Track Record.
